`repo-familiar` is a **Project Generator** and **Reference Source** for reusable **Agentic Engineering Defaults**. It creates self-contained **Downstream Repositories** and supports preview-first adoption in existing repositories.

## Start Here

- New to the project? Complete [Generate Your First Repository](./tutorials/generate-first-repository.qmd).
- Generating a configured repository? Use [Generate a Repository](./how-to/generate-repository.qmd).
- Adopting defaults in existing work? Use [Bootstrap an Existing Repository](./how-to/bootstrap-existing-repository.qmd).
- Looking up exact behavior? Start with the [CLI and Metadata Reference](./reference/cli-and-metadata.qmd) or [Bootstrap Lifecycle](./reference/bootstrap-lifecycle.qmd).
- Trying to understand the design? Read [Architecture](./explanation/architecture.qmd) and the [Documentation System](./explanation/documentation-system.qmd).

## Project Authorities

Use each source for its intended question:

| Question | Authority |
|---|---|
| What does the product mean and exclude? | [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/ewheeler/repo-familiar/blob/main/CONTEXT.md) |
| What is implemented or planned now? | [`PLAN.md`](https://github.com/ewheeler/repo-familiar/blob/main/PLAN.md) |
| Why was a durable choice made? | [Decisions and ADRs](./project-record/decisions.qmd) |
| Which module and test own a change? | [Repository Map](./project-record/repository-map.md) |
| What does the executable currently do? | Source and tests, routed through the repository map |

Plans and ADRs can describe work that is not yet implemented. Confirm availability in current source and tests.

## Documentation Shape

The sidebar follows the Divio documentation system:

- **Tutorials** teach through a complete, reliable learning path.
- **How-to guides** solve a specific task.
- **Reference** records exact commands, contracts, and configuration.
- **Explanation** records architecture, tradeoffs, and opinions.
- **Project Record** groups plans, decisions, research, requirements, and agent routing while retaining one of the four documentation types.
